en: One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Prophecy of Kṣemadatta*,
compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhisheng of Chongfu Monastery during the Tang Dynasty; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei Dynasty.
*The Sūtra on Neither Increasing nor Decreasing*, one fascicle; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei. *The Sūtra on the Merit of Building Stūpas*, one fascicle;

translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīladharma of Central India during the Tang dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Merit of Circumambulating Buddha Stūpas*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty. *The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Four Dharmas*, one fascicle;

translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty. *The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Questions of the Virtuous Daughter*, one fascicle; [translated] during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty.

*Mahāyāna-saṃsāra-sattva-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the [Tang] era; *Rājñaḥ Suvarṇavarṇa-vyatikara-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang;
*Buddhabhāṣita-sāgarakulaputra-dharmamudrā-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang;

*Siṃhasauḍasa-rāja-māṃsa-pratiṣedha-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìyán of Zhìxiàng Monastery during the Tang; *Parinirvāṇa-guālā-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated during the Western Jin dynasty.

*The Scripture of the Names of Eight Classes of Buddhas*, one fascicle, translated by Zhu Fahu of the Three Piṭakas; *The Scripture on the Bodhisattva’s Practice of the Six Pāramitās*, one fascicle, translated by the śramaṇa Yan Fotiao of Linhuai during the Later Han;

and *The Account of the Bodhisattva Casting Himself to a Starving Tiger and the Subsequent Erection of a Stūpa*, translated by Gautama Prajñāruci, a Brāhmaṇa of the Northern Wei—these twenty-two scriptures, totaling twenty-two fascicles, are contained in the same volume, comprising one hundred and forty-eight sheets.

*Yuanjing* (Scripture on Conditions), one fascicle; translated by the monk Fa-sheng of Gaochang during the Northern Liang dynasty. *Jingang Sanmei Benxing Qingjing Bubai Bumie Jing* (Sūtra on the Vajrasamādhi, the Innate Purity, Indestructibility, and Immortality), one fascicle;

translator lost. *Shiziyue Fobenxing Jing* (Sūtra on the Previous Birth of Siṃhacandra Buddha), one fascicle; translator lost. *Zhangzhe Fazhi Qi Jing* (Sūtra on the Wife of the Householder Dharmasena), one fascicle; translator lost. *Saguo Jing* (Sūtra of the Country of Sāla), one fascicle; translator lost. *Shijixiang Jing* (Sūtra of the Ten Auspiciousnesses), one fascicle.

*Zhangzhenü Andicheshenhao Liao yi Jing* (Sūtra on the Lion’s Roar of the Meaning of Definitive Truth by the Daughter of the Householder Andhika), one fascicle. *Yiqiezhi Guangming Xianren Cixin Yinyuan Bushi* (The Causes and Conditions of the Compassionate Heart of the Rishi Sarvavid-āloka-ketu, Not Eating... [incomplete].

*The Sūtra on Meat*, one fascicle; four sūtras, all lost translations. *The Vajrasamādhi Sūtra*, two fascicles; lost translation during the Northern Liang dynasty. *The Sūtra on the Extinction of the Dharma*, one fascicle; listed among the lost translations in Sengyou’s catalog.

*The Sūtra of the Profound Great Dedication*, one fascicle; listed among the lost translations in Sengyou’s catalog. *The Sūtra of the Prince of the Heavenly King, Piluo*, one fascicle; Sengyou’s catalog states it was an "extraordinary sūtra" (yijing) from Guanzhong by Master Dao’an.

*The Sūtra on the Dharma-gate of Pure Conduct for Upāli*, two fascicles; listed as an "extraordinary sūtra" in Sengyou’s catalog. Eight [sūtras] concerning the Mahāsattvas produced in the Liang region by Master Dao’an.

*Jue jing* (Sūtra on Awakening), one fascicle; translated by An Shigao, Tripiṭaka Master of Parthia during the Later Han. *Sanpin dishi jing* (Sūtra on the Three Grades of Disciples), one fascicle; translated by Zhi Qian, Upāsaka of Yuezhi during the Wu. *Sishi jing* (Sūtra on the Four Classes [of Disciples]), one fascicle;

translated by Zhu Fahu, Tripiṭaka Master of the Western Jin. *Danglai bian jing* (Sūtra on Future Transformations), one fascicle; translated by Zhu Fahu, Tripiṭaka Master of the Western Jin. *Guoqu fo fenwei jing* (Sūtra on the Past Buddha’s Almsround), one fascicle;
translated by Zhu Fahu, Tripiṭaka Master of the Western Jin. *Shier toutuo jing* (Sūtra on the Twelve Dhūtas), one fascicle; translated by Guṇabhadra, Tripiṭaka Master from India during the Song.

*Śuddhipanthaka Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Guṇabhadra. *Rājarṣi Dīrghāyu Sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Sengyou Lu* states it was a lost translation by Master Dao’an. *Dharmasthitinirdeśa Sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Sengyou Lu* states it was a lost translation by Master Dao’an. The above twenty-three sūtras comprise twenty-five fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred forty-three pages. *Bodhisattvavinaya-piṭaka*, twenty-six sections in fifty-four fascicles across five volumes. *Bodhisattvabhūmi-vidhi-sūtra*, eight fascicles; also known as the *Bhūmividyā-śāstra*. Translated at Guzang by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang dynasty. This single volume of eight fascicles totals one hundred ninety-one pages. *The Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra*, ten fascicles; also known as *The Bodhisattva-bhūmi*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇavarman of Kasmīra during the Song dynasty, etc. *The Sūtra on Purifying Karmic Obstructions*, one fascicle; translator lost. These two preceding sūtras comprise eleven fascicles in a single volume, totaling 207 sheets. [Xian].

The *Upāsaka-śīla-sūtra* in seven fascicles: the bodhisattva precepts for laypeople, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang dynasty at Guzang. The *Brahmajāla-sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. The *Daśakuśala-karma-patha-upadeśa-sūtra* in one fascicle, translator lost during the Later Han dynasty. These three sūtras comprise ten fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and ninety-four pages. [Ke].
*The Bodhisattva’s Ornament of the Original Vows Sūtra*, two fascicles; alternatively, without the word "Bodhisattva. Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin dynasty.

*The Buddha-treasury Sūtra*, four fascicles; also titled *The Explanation of All Dharmas*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva during the Yao Qin dynasty. *Bodhisattva Precepts Text*, one fascicle. Extracted from the *Bhūmivastu* chapter, spoken by Maitreya Bodhisattva.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang dynasty. *Bodhisattva Precepts Text*, one fascicle. Extracted from the *Bodhisattvabhūmi* within the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*, spoken by Maitreya. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master [Xuanzang] of the Tang dynasty.

*The Ritual Text for the Bodhisattva Precepts*, one fascicle, translated by Xuanzang; excerpted from the "Bodhisattvabhūmi" within the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* (spoken by Maitreya Bodhisattva), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty.

*The Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra*, one fascicle, spoken by Maitreya Bodhisattva and translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *The Method for Receiving the Bodhisattva Precepts as Asked by Upāli*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇavarman of Kasmira during the Song dynasty.
These six scriptures comprise ten fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and seventy-four pages.

*The Bodhisattva’s Inner Precepts Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇavarman of Kaśmīra during the Song dynasty. *The Upāsaka’s Five Precepts and Dignified Conduct Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇavarman of Kaśmīra during the Song dynasty.
*Mañjuśrī’s Pure Vinaya Sūtra*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *Pure Vinaya Sūtra*; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.

*The Extensive Vinaya of Purity Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *The Sūtra of the Questions of Śāntasvara*, one fascicle; also known as *The Tathāgata’s...* [text fragment].

*Śuddhaviśuddhavinaya-sūtra*, translated by the Song dynasty śramaṇa Shi Fǎhǎi; *Mahāyāna-triskandhaka-pratideśana-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Sui dynasty Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others;
*Bodhisattva-pañcadharma-pratideśana*, one fascicle—also called *Bodhisattva-pañcadharma-pratideśana-sūtra*—translator lost;

*Bodhisattvapiṭaka-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Liang dynasty Funan Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman; *Samantabhadrotsāhana-bodhisattva-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Western Jin dynasty lay believer Nie Dàozhēn; *Bodhi-* [text continues].

*Sāshòu zhāijīng* (Sutra on Receiving the Fast), one fascicle; translated by the Western Jin lay devotee Nie Daozhen. *Wénshū huìguò jīng* (Sutra of Mañjuśrī’s Repentance), one fascicle; also titled *Wénshū wǔtǐ huìguò jīng* (Sutra of Mañjuśrī’s Five-Part Repentance);

translated by the Western Jin Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa. *Shèlìfù huìguò jīng* (Sutra of Śāriputra’s Repentance), one fascicle; also simply titled *Huìguò jīng* (Sutra of Repentance); translated by the Later Han Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia.

*Fǎlǜ sānmèi jīng* (Sutra on the Samādhi of Dharma and Discipline), one fascicle; also simply titled *Fǎlǜ jīng* (Sutra of Dharma and Discipline); translated by the Wu Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhi Qian. *Shíshàn yèdào jīng* (Sutra of the Path of Ten Wholesome Deeds).

One fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang dynasty. The fourteen scriptures above comprise fourteen fascicles, totaling one hundred fifty-five sheets.

The *Bodhisattvapitakadharmaparyāya* consists of ninety-seven sections and five hundred eighteen fascicles, arranged in fifty bundles. The Mahāyāna commentaries on the sūtras consist of twenty-one works totaling one hundred fifty-five fascicles, arranged in fifteen bundles. The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* consists of one hundred fascicles—or alternatively one hundred ten or seventy—translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. From the first bundle to the tenth, it totals two thousand one hundred fifty-five sheets. [Seal] [Holy] [Virtue] [Established] [Name] [Set] [Form] [Upright] [Manifest] [Correct] [Emptiness].

*Daśabhūmika-sūtra-śāstra*, twelve fascicles (or fifteen fascicles), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty and others; one volume comprising approximately two hundred and fifty sheets. [Gu]。

The *Mahāyāna-sūtrālaṃkāra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Questions of Maitreya Bodhisattva), six fascicles—alternatively recorded as six or seven or ten fascicles—translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei. The *Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Mahāyāna Ratnakūṭa Sūtra), four fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei. The *Ratnacūḍa-bodhisattva-caturdharma-sūtra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Ratnacūḍa Bodhisattva’s Sūtra of the Four Dharmas), one fascicle, composed by Vasubandhu Bodhisattva; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Vimalamitra and others of the Northern Wei. The above three treatises comprise eleven fascicles in a single volume, totaling two hundred twenty-four sheets. [Biographical Account].

*Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya-vajracchedikā-sūtra-śāstra-kārikā*, one fascicle; also known as *Vajracchedikā-śāstra*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yi Jing of the Tang Dynasty. *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, three fascicles. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmagupta of the Sui Dynasty. *Buddhabhūmi-sūtra-śāstra*, seven fascicles. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. The above three treatises comprise eleven fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and seventy pages. [Śeng].
*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra Śāstra*, three fascicles; composed by Bodhisattva Vasubandhu, translated by Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei.
*Treatise on the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, three fascicles; verses by Bodhisattva Asaṅga, commentary by Bodhisattva Vasubandhu.
*The Treatise on Destroying Attachment and Not Destroying Provisional Names to the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, two fascicles, translated by Tripitaka Master Yijing of the Tang;

also known as the *Treatise on Merit*, composed by Bodhisattva Guṇadatta and translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara of Central India. *The Treatise on the Sūtra of the Questions of Śuśīla Bodhisattva Concerning Bodhi*, two fascicles, also titled the *Gayāśīrṣa Sūtra*; composed by Bodhisattva Vasubandhu.
The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-śāstra*, one fascicle, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei; composed by the Bodhisattva Vasubandhu.

Translated together with Senglang and others by the Tripiṭaka Master Ratnamati of Central India of the Northern Wei. The above five treatises comprise eleven fascicles and total one hundred and seventy-nine sheets.
[Marked as "Xū"].

*The Commentary on the Lotus Sūtra*, two fascicles; the first contains a verse of homage, or [alternatively] one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of North India during the Northern Wei, together with Tanlin and others. *The Treatise on the Questions of the Brahma God Vimati*, four fascicles (or three fascicles); translated by Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei. *The Treatise on Nirvāṇa*, one fascicle; a brief explanation of *Nirvāṇa*; composed by the Bodhisattva Vasubandhu; translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmapriya of the Northern Wei. *Treatise on the Verses of Original Existence and Present Non-existence from the Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, one fascicle;

an explanation of a single verse from the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Liang dynasty. *Treatise on the Sūtra of the Buddha’s Bequeathed Teaching*, one fascicle; the new translation of the *Sūtra of the Buddha’s Bequeathed Teaching*; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Chen dynasty. *Treatise on the Sūtra of Immeasurable Life*, one fascicle; explained by Vasubandhu.

*Tri-samaya-sūtra-śāstra*, one fascicle; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei dynasty. Contains the commentary but lacks the sūtra text. Composed by Vasubandhu Bodhisattva;

translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Masters Vimokṣaprajña and others of the Northern Wei dynasty. *Dharmacakra-pravartana-sūtra-śāstra*, one fascicle; contains the commentary but lacks the original sūtra text. Composed by Vasubandhu Bodhisattva;

translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Masters Vimokṣaprajña and others of the Northern Wei dynasty. The above eight treatises comprise twelve fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and sixty-five sheets.

[Hall]. *Mahāyāna-saṃgraha-artha-śāstra* (Treatise on the Collected Meanings of the Mahāyāna), seventy-six works in three hundred and sixty-three fascicles, fifteen bundles. *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* (Treatise on the Stages of Yoga Practice), one hundred fascicles, expounded by Maitreya Bodhisattva; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty, ten bundles, totaling one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five sheets. [Practice] [Listen] [Calamity] [Cause] [Evil] [Accumulation] [Merit] [Condition] [Goodness] [Celebration].
The *Prakaraṇāryavācā-śāstra* (Treatise on the Manifestation of the Noble Teachings), twenty fascicles, composed by Bodhisattva Asaṅga;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. Two bundles, totaling three hundred and thirty-eight sheets. [Cheng] [Bi].
*Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra-vyākhyā*, one fascicle; composed by Bodhisattvas such as Jinaputra.
Translated by the Tang Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang. *Tattvārtha-śāstra*, one fascicle; composed by Maitreya Bodhisattva.

Translated by the Tang Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang. *Mahāyānābhidharma-samuccaya-śāstra*, seven fascicles; composed by Asaṅga Bodhisattva. Translated by the Tang Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang. The above four treatises comprise ten fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and forty-nine sheets. [Non-Buddhist].

The *Mahāyānābhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā* (Great Vehicle Abhidharma Compendium Commentary), sixteen fascicles, compiled by the Bodhisattva Sthiramati; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. The *Madhyamakaśāstra* (Treatise on the Middle Way), four fascicles, originally composed by the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna and commented upon by the Brahmin Candrakīrti; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin Dynasty. These two treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two volumes, totaling three hundred and fifty-nine sheets. [Bǎo] [Cùn].

*Prajñāpradīpa-śāstra-vyākhyā*, fifteen fascicles; composed by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna, commentary by Bodhisattva Bhāviveka; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prabhākaramitra of India during the Tang dynasty. *Dvādaśamukha-śāstra*, one fascicle; composed by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yaoqin dynasty. *Aṣṭadaśaśūnyatā-śāstra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Chen dynasty. *Śata-śāstra*, two fascicles; composed by Bodhisattva Āryadeva, commentary by the Bodhisattva Vasu; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yaoqin dynasty. *Viṃśatikā-śāstra*, one fascicle; composed by Bodhisattva Āryadeva; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. The above five treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two volumes, totaling three hundred and sixty-six sheets. [Category: Skandhas] [Is].

The Commentary on the Extensive Hundred-Verse Treatise of the Mahāyāna (Mahāyāna-śataka-vṛtti), ten fascicles; composed by Āryadeva and commented upon by Dharmapāla; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. From one bundle, totaling one hundred and thirteen sheets. [Jing].

*Daśabhūmivibhāṣā-śāstra*, fifteen fascicles, composed by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Bodhicaryāvatāra-prakaraṇa* (or *Bodhi-sambhāra-śāstra*), six fascicles, original text by the Venerable Nāgārjuna; commentary by the Bhikṣu Īśvara; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Dharmagupta. The above two treatises comprise twenty-one fascicles in two volumes, totaling three hundred and seventy-five sheets. [Zi] [Fu].

The Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra-śāstra, in thirteen fascicles (or fifteen fascicles), composed by Asaṅga; translated by the Tang Dynasty Indian Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha. From one bundle, totaling two hundred and eleven pages. [Section on Matters].

*Mahāvyūha-sūtra-śāstra*, fifteen fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Madhyamaka-anupūrva-śāstra*, two fascicles; translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of the Yuan Wei dynasty. *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-śāstra*, three fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Chen dynasty. These three treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two volumes, totaling three hundred and one sheets. [The Preface] says:

The *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-śāstra* in two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhāśanta of India during the Northern Wei Dynasty; the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-mūla* in three fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty; and the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya* in fifteen fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Chen Dynasty. The Sanskrit name is *Kulata*, which in the Chen language means "intimate reliance," or alternatively *Paramārtha*, which means "True Meaning. These three treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two volumes, totaling five hundred and twenty-three sheets. [Yan] [Yu].
The *Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya*, ten fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty; from one bundle, totaling one hundred and fifty-nine sheets. [Jing].
The *Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya*, ten fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. From one bundle of ten fascicles, totaling one hundred eighty-four sheets. [Kǎo].

*Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya*, ten fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. Totaling two hundred twenty-seven sheets from one bundle. 【Dang】. *Buddhadhātuśāstra*, four fascicles;

translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Chen dynasty. *Viniscayasamgrahaṇī*, three fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Liang dynasty. *Madhyāntavibhāgakārikā*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Madhyāntavibhāga-bhāṣya*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Chen dynasty. These four treatises comprise ten fascicles in the same bundle, totaling one hundred eighty-six sheets. 【Jie】.

*Madhyāntavibhāga-kārikā* (Verses on the Discrimination of the Middle and the Extremes), three fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Ratnagotravibhāga-mahāyānottaratantra-śāstra* (The Ultimate One Vehicle Jewel Nature Treatise), five fascicles; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Ratnamati of the Northern Wei dynasty. *Karmasiddhi-prakaraṇa* (Treatise on the Accomplishment of Karma), one fascicle; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Vimokṣaprajña and others of the Northern Wei dynasty. *Mahāyāna-karmasiddhi-śāstra* (Treatise on the Accomplishment of Karma in the Mahāyāna), one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Nyāyamukha-śāstra* (The Entrance Gate for Logic), one fascicle; composed by Bodhisattva Śrīlāta. [Recorded in the *Chus neidian lu*] Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. The above five treatises comprise eleven fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and seventy-five pages. 【Li】.

*Hetuvidyānyāyamukha-śāstra*, one fascicle. Newly included in the canon as the second translation of the *Nyāyamukha-śāstra*. Originally recorded by Zhou as a single work, newly examined and identified as a re-translation. Composed by Bodhisattva Śubhagupta.

*The Treatise on Entering into Correct Logic* (Nyāyapraveśa-śāstra), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of the Tang Dynasty, Yijing. *The Treatise on Manifesting Consciousness* (Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-viṃśatikā-kārikā), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of Ceylon during the Chen Dynasty. *The Treatise on the Transformation of Consciousness* (Vijñānapariṇāma-śāstra), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of Ceylon during the Chen Dynasty. *The Mahāyāna Treatise on Consciousness-Only*, one fascicle, translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei. *The Mahāyāna Treatise on Consciousness-Only*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of Ceylon during the Chen Dynasty. *The Twenty Verses on Consciousness-Only* (Vijñaptimātratā-siddhi-viṃśatikā-kārikā), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. *The Jewel-Arising Commentary on the Establishment of Consciousness-Only* (Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-alaṃkāra-śāstra), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty. *The Thirty Verses on Consciousness-Only* (Triṃśikā-vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-kārikā), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. The above nine treatises comprise thirteen fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and forty-nine sheets. [Zhong]
*Cheng weishi lun* (Treatise on the Establishment of Consciousness-Only), ten fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty;

one bundle, totaling one hundred and eighty-five sheets. [Ce] *Tze dafu lun* (Treatise on the Great Man), two fascicles, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Daotai of the Northern Liang Dynasty; *Ruru ruzheng lun* (Treatise on Entering the Mahāyāna), two fascicles, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Daotai of the Northern Liang Dynasty; *Dasheng zhangzhen lun* (Mahāyāna-Śata-śāstra), two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty; *Dasheng wuyun lun* (Mahāyāna-Pañcaskandhaka-śāstra), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty; *Dasheng guangwuyun lun* (Extensive Mahāyāna-Pañcaskandhaka-śāstra), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jīvaka of Central India during the Tang Dynasty; *Baohang wangzheng lun* (Ratnāvalī), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Chen Dynasty; *Dasheng qixin lun* (Mahāyāna-Śraddhotpāda-śāstra), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Liang Dynasty. These seven treatises comprise ten fascicles in the same bundle, totaling one hundred and eighty-five sheets. [Jin]

*Mahāyāna-śraddhotpāda-śāstra*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the Tang dynasty. *Bodhicittotpāda-śāstra*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. *Dvayanairātmya-śāstra*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty. *Upāyahṛdaya-śāstra*, one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Kiṅkara together with Tanyao of the Northern Wei dynasty. *Tattvasiddhi-śāstra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of the Liang dynasty. *Nirākāravijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty. *Ālambanaparīkṣā-śāstra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty. *Ālambanaparīkṣāvṛtti*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang dynasty. The above eight treatises comprise eleven fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and fifty-one pages. [Section on Life].

*Vigrahavyāvartanī-śāstra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vimokṣasena et al. of the Northern Wei. *Pratītyasamutpāda-śāstra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmagupta of the Sui. *Dvādaśāṅga-pratītyasamutpāda-śāstra*, one fascicle;

translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei. *Ekottarika-śāstra*, one fascicle; translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei. *Mahāyāna-śata-dharma-viśada-mukha-śāstra*, one fascicle;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang. *Śata-akṣara-śāstra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei.

*Jiejuan jing* (Sūtra on the Unrolling of the Scroll), translated by Zhi [Qian], one fascicle; *Nan zuo lun* (Treatise on Making South), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of the Chen Dynasty, one fascicle; *Zhongzhong lun* (Treatise on the Palm), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty, one fascicle; *Quyin jiashelun* (Treatise on the Assumption of Causes), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty, one fascicle;

*Guanzongsiang lun song* (Verses on the Treatise Examining General Characteristics), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty, one fascicle; *Zhiguanmen lun song* (Verses on the Treatise on the Gates of Calming and Contemplation), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty, one fascicle;

*Shouzhang lun* (Treatise on the Staff), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty, one fascicle; *Liumen jiaoshou xiding lun* (Treatise on the Six Gates for Teaching the Practice of Concentration), translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty, one fascicle.

*Mahāyāna-dharmadhātu-abhedha-śāstra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tang Tripiṭaka Master Ti-yun Prajñā of Khotan. *Nirākaraṇa-tīrthika-hīnayāna-catur-nikāya-śāstra*, one fascicle, translated by the Northern Wei Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India.
*Nirākaraṇa-tīrthika-hīnayāna-nirvāṇa-śāstra*, one fascicle, translated by the Northern Wei Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India.
The above sixteen treatises comprise sixteen fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and twelve sheets.

In total, including all Mahāyāna sūtras, vinayas, and śāstras currently in circulation, there are six hundred and thirty-eight works comprising two thousand seven hundred and forty-five fascicles, arranged in two hundred and fifty-eight bundles.
Abridged Extract from the Kaiyuan Catalogue of Buddhist Teachings, Scroll Two, Part Two.
